prompt: A warm-lit straight-on photograph of a guitar-method book page on a stand showing one short TAB (tablature) riff. Draw the six horizontal tab lines with the letters T A B stacked at the left. Along the lines, from left to right in time, write these fret numbers on these strings (string 1 is the TOP line, string 6 the BOTTOM line): 3 on string 1, 5 on string 2, 2 on string 3, 0 on string 1, 7 on string 4, 3 on string 2, 8 on string 5. Each number sits exactly on its own string line, evenly spaced. Crisp black print on real paper, no chord boxes, no other numbers.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show guitar-method book page on a stand showing a single-line TAB riff (six tab lines with fret numbers) under warm light, straight-on photo? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_seq: This is guitar TAB (tablature): 6 horizontal lines; the TOP line is string 1 (thinnest / highest) and the BOTTOM line is string 6 (thickest / lowest). Each printed number is a fret played on the line it sits on, read left to right. For EACH number give 'string:fret' where string is 1 (top) to 6 (bottom) and fret is the printed number. List all separated by commas. Read ONLY what is printed: each number together with the line it sits on; do NOT guess at the music. If unreadable answer 'unreadable'.
